beliefs.practice: Read the MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; use that to create a MongoClient with TLS/ssl enabled, reasonable timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS and connectTimeoutMS), and a bounded connection pool (maxPoolSize) appropriate for the app's concurrency.

Keep secrets out of the repo: put the DocumentDB URI and any LLM/API keys in environment variables or a secrets store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) and provide only a .env.example with placeholders in the repo.
Make seed operations idempotent by using a deterministic unique key (e.g., company_id) and upsert/replace_one with upsert=True rather than blind inserts so repeated runs don't create duplicates.
Store E, S, G scores as small integers (1-10) and store a precomputed normalized composite_score field in each document to support fast sorting/aggregation instead of recomputing in every query.

Store the LLM rationale text and a separate embedding vector field (e.g., rationale_embedding: [float]) in the same document; keep vector field name and embedding dimension consistent across documents and persist type as float32 arrays (or BSON arrays of floats).

Create appropriate indexes for the queries the app runs: at minimum an index on composite_score (descending) to support ranking, plus indexes on company_id (unique) and any fields used in filters (e.g., sector); create compound indexes when queries filter+sort on multiple fields.

For semantic/vector search, create a server-side vector index on the embedding field with parameters matching the index type (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN), the correct dimension, and the chosen distance metric; ensure the index's dimension matches the embedding model exactly.

Normalize or L2-normalize embeddings at write time if you intend to use cosine similarity with the vector index; alternatively, use whatever metric (dot/cosine/Euclidean) the index expects—do not mix metrics between stored vectors and query-time similarity.

When creating vector indexes, include index parameters (e.g., M/efConstruction for HNSW or nlist/nprobe for IVF) tuned for production query latency/recall, and create them during a controlled maintenance window because building vector indexes can be resource-intensive.

Use bulk writes (bulk_write with ordered=False) when seeding many documents to improve throughput and set write concern appropriately; handle BulkWriteError and inspect result.upserted_ids for idempotency verification.

Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network or rate-limit errors (handle MongoNetworkError, MongoServerSelectionError, and 429/TooManyRequests) and make operations idempotent where possible (use upserts and idempotent document updates).

Provision database/collection throughput (RUs) or enable autoscale to support vector search and embedding-upsert workloads; monitor RU consumption and increase throughput if index builds or searches are throttled (watch for 429s).

Avoid very large documents: keep each document well under the service's per-document size limit (use referenced documents or grid storage for very large blobs) so vector fields + text + metadata don't exceed the limit.

When updating embeddings or scores, write the embedding and composite_score in a single atomic update to avoid inconsistency between score and rationale_embedding (use single-document update/upsert to preserve atomicity).

Store a last_updated timestamp and a version or processing_status field on each document so the processing pipeline can resume, avoid reprocessing already-scored docs, and support idempotent re-run logic.

Use aggregation pipeline stages efficiently: pre-filter documents in $match before $addFields/$project and use $sort with covered index on composite_score to avoid in-memory sorts; paginate with $skip/$limit or better with range queries on a sorted field.

Restrict network access to the DocumentDB cluster (firewall rules, VNet/private endpoint) and create least-privilege database users/roles for the app instead of using the account-level master key in app code.

Instrument the app with diagnostics and metrics: enable Azure diagnostic logs and request/operation metrics, log slow queries and index build activity, and monitor RU usage and 429 throttling to tune indexes and throughput.

Prefer storing embeddings as arrays on the document rather than as separate collection documents when using server-side vector indexes, because vector indexes typically index a scalar/vector field on the same document the app queries and sorted/filtered by metadata fields.

In tests and development, use small synthetic datasets and a TTL index or test-only database to avoid consuming production throughput or polluting production data; make seed and teardown scripts idempotent and safe to run repeatedly.
